newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish leasors expect 40-50 pct growth in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Turkish leasors expect 40-50 pct growth in 1997.

text.p: Turkey's leasing sector is expected to continue its rapid growth and aims to raise 1997 turnover by 40-50 percent in dollar terms, sector officials said.

"In 1997 we expect a 40-50 percent growth in dollar terms in the leasing sector. Number of leasing companies are rising and this instrument is now known in Turkey," said Bulent Tasar, vice-president of the association of leasing companies.
"Total volume was around $1.6 billion in 1996 and is expected to reach $2.4 billion this year," Tasar told Reuters.
Share of the leasing sector in financing total fixed investments is expected to reach 10 percent levels in 1997, from around six percent in 1996, he added.
"There is an appetite for investments in Turkey although some problems exist, like difficulty in securing medium and long-term loans," Tasar said.
"But by securing World bank and Eximbank type loans in 1996, the leasing sector managed to extend the maturities of the available funds and started to finance bigger projects ," he added.
Ertugrul Yurdacan, general manager of Vakif Leasing said the average maturity of funds used in the sector was extended to five years from two in 1996.
"We can easily find loans of up to five years from Eximbanks outside Turkey and are able to sell at the same maturities to our customers," Yurdacan said.
Of the five leasing companies listed on the Istanbul Stock Exchange, four of them announced real increases in 1996 net profits. About 51 leasing companies operate in Turkey.
